title: Mitosis core re-spec (new SPEC, zero dependency on 2026-07-30)

completion_criteria.text: Scope modifications for the new SPEC are decided with the user and recorded as a decision record.
Brainstorming run in a FRESH session via superpowers:brainstorming before any SPEC drafting begins.
SPEC A (config staging/live promotion) authored standalone - no inherited decision numbers, no step-N chain, no citation of the 2026-07-30 document as authority.
User reviews SPEC A and approves it, before any SPEC B drafting begins.
SPEC B (mitosis core: token/latency cost, codegen decomposition, stacked PRs) authored standalone, with the fix pipeline excluded and no citation of the 2026-07-30 document as authority.
User reviews SPEC B and approves it.

spine.active_goal: Author SPEC A standalone from the approved design: a staging/live config split whose promotion is atomic and whose sync is enforced rather than suggested.
spine.next_step: Fresh session: author SPEC A from the approved design in the 2026-08-06T20-17 session event plus decisions 0269 and 0270. The design is APPROVED - do NOT re-brainstorm it. Write it standalone to docs/superpowers/specs/, run the brainstorming spec self-review, then hand it to the user for the c4 review gate. Settle the mid-session swap measurement only if implementation turns out to need it.
spine.last_session: Approved approach A, settled the SPEC A design across seven sections, and recorded decisions 0269 and 0270. No spec document written.

open_risks.text: Instrument per-dispatch context before trusting any collapse win — the 2026-07-30 plan counts dispatches and wall-clock only, so Decompose fusion, Ship 13-to-1, and per-MSP reviews would all score as wins even if cost rose.

Re-derive every line citation from the current tree — mitosis.js is 5,515 lines against the cited 4,851, the phase-parity gate appears already landed, and mitosis-git.mjs moved to .claude/lib/git/pr.mjs.
Decide telemetry before making any cost claim — no token or tool-call accounting exists anywhere in the engine, so every re-exploration claim is unmeasurable today.

Do not re-run the three investigations — the engine map, stacked-PR research and config inventory cost roughly 340k subagent tokens, their transcripts do not survive, and the 2026-08-06T19-31 session event is the only remaining copy.

The promote verb and the SessionStart hook must live outside releases/ — a bootstrap self-hosted in the thing it promotes means a bad release breaks the machinery that would roll it back, in every future session. This is the one way the design can brick the environment.

Promote only at SessionStart or between MSPs, never mid-MSP — immutable releases stop any single file being read half-old, but a running session can still hold one release's skill roster while reading another's bodies, and retention cannot fix that because reads route through the pointer.

The swap must be create-then-rename, not ln -sfn — ln -sfn unlinks then symlinks and leaves a window with no pointer, and the live permission set grants Bash(ln -sfn:*), so it currently encodes the wrong form.

Whether a pointer swap reaches an already-running session is still unmeasured — headless claude cannot authenticate under a scratch config dir, so the promotion-timing contract rests on an untested assumption.

Only one settings.json writer was measured — if in-session /config edits or permission-grant persistence replace the file rather than write through it, the ownership manifest still holds but the file-identity assumption behind it needs re-checking.
parallel-plan-execution.js is dead code — its top-level dynamic imports cannot execute in the Workflow runtime, so any design routing work through it builds on a broken entry point.

key_decisions.title: Dependent MSP chains merge with merge-commit; standalone PRs keep squash
Workflow runtime forbids dynamic import, so codegen is the only path off the twinning tax
Split the re-spec into two specs, config promotion landing before the mitosis core
Config promotion is an immutable release subtree plus an atomic pointer rename, with live pinned to main
settings.json is excluded from releases and reconciled by an ownership manifest, with the leak gate on capture only
SPEC B is authored next in a fresh session, SPEC A is implemented before SPEC B, and SPEC B leads with the cost instrument

out_of_scope: Implementing any MSP from either SPEC
Editing mitosis.js, the parallel engine, or any live config path while a SPEC is being authored
